newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS CHASE TWICKENHAM DREAM.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PUMAS CHASE TWICKENHAM DREAM.

text.p: The Pumas are planning to catch England unawares at Twickenham on Saturday and prove to the world there is more to Argentine rugby than a beefy set of forwards.

One of the last bastions of amateurism in the newly professional rugby world, Argentina suffered two heavy home defeats to South Africa last month and lost 51-0 on their only test visit to Twickenham in 1990.
But the Pumas' coaching staff and captain Lisandro Arbizu insist a new era is about to dawn and hope the encounter with England will confirm the current team are headed in the right direction.

"What we are looking for is to change the style of Argentine rugby," confirmed coach Jose Luis Imhoff, working closely on this tour with former All Black Alex "Grizz" Wyllie, hired as 'technical advisor'.
"With the help of Alex, I think we're going to see the birth of a new type of Argentine rugby which will enable us to compete with the best teams in the world.
"After this test we'll be able to say whether this year has been positive or negative, or whether we have stayed the same."
The Pumas scored seven tries against France during two tests in June, and beat Canada, the United States and Uruguay in the Pan-American Cup in September.

They also outscored the English two tries to nil in Durban during last year's World Cup, only to lose 24-18, and Wyllie believes there is more than enough potential to offset the unavailability of world-class front-row men Federico Mendez and Patricio Noriega.
"I believe this pack can stand up to the best of them. I think they're good at set pieces, but it's learning to make better use of the ball they win that's crucial," said Wyllie.
"One of the biggest problems is keeping them focused on the game for 80 minutes. They've got ability, but sometimes they lose their focus which lets good teams in"
A decent result would certainly help Wyllie, generously described as "the best coach in the world" by Imhoff on Thursday, to negotiate an extension to his current short-term contract.
Arbizu, one of six Argentine survivors from the Durban encounter, will be doing his best to assist, if only to grab some of the headlines away from his pack.
"We are going to play as props so we can receive some of the compliments they get," joked the 25-year-old centre.
"I think we have very powerful backs and we want to show it on Saturday. We must believe in ourselves and show we can play against anyone."
With Phil de Glanville sidelined by a leg strain, England will be led by prop Jason Leonard who won the first of his 50 caps against Argentina in 1990.
Another debutant that day was Gonzalo Camardon at scrum-half for the Pumas. He reappears this time on the right wing.

England - 15-Nick Beal; 14-Jon Sleightholme,13-Will Carling, 12-Jeremy Guscott, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Andy Gomarsall; 8-Chris Sheasby, 7-Lawrence Dallaglio, 6-Tim Rodber, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Martin Johnson, 3-Jason Leonard, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Argentina - 15-Ezequiel Jurado; 14-Gonzalo Camardon, 13-Eduardo Simone, 12-Lisandro Arbizu (captain), 11-Diego Albanese; 10-Gonzalo Quesada, 9-Nicolas Fernandez Miranda; 8-Pablo Bouza, 7-Pablo Camerlinckx, 6-Rolando Martin, 5-German Llanes, 4-Pedro Sporleder, 3-Mauricio Reggiardo, 2-Carlos Promanzio, 1-Roberto Grau.
